_meta.what_this_is: One row of a high-resolution image, to be downsampled by 2. The row is a smooth brightness gradient (the real scene we want to keep) plus a fine one-pixel checkerboard texture (+6, -6, +6, ... -- detail too fine to survive at half resolution). The gradient is what a correct downscale should preserve; the checker should average away to nothing. The row is built so the checker sits exactly at the Nyquist frequency, where naive every-other-pixel decimation aliases it into a false uniform brightness shift instead of averaging it out.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. gradient + checker are given separately so the ideal downsample is exact and checkable; 'row' is their sum, the actual pixels.
_meta.format: factor; gradient [...]; checker [...]; row [...] = gradient + checker
